recommendation.reason: Installed help and matching source prove --no-recursive exists; this avoids default source closure traversal and avoids even a temporary substituters override. Destination registration still requires all real refs. Do not use default recursive copy with a one-entry cache.

findings.conclusion: Use unchanged official nix-cache-info with StoreDir:/nix/store; exact 5zv6ms4i0bqpngarnp24h188936mv3sv.narinfo bytes at cache root; exact original relative URL nar/0wvg24krj0ryky8gyjpwzh746cx2digqcjlvg7lv8vxif6v5y7i0.nar.zst under that root. No rewriting narinfo/signature or recompression. Binary cache file:// is distinct from a plain chroot store path.

Original signature remains applicable at a different cache location: signed fingerprint is version1;StorePath;NarHash;NarSize;References. URL/Compression/FileHash/FileSize/Deriver are outside fingerprint, hence full compressed FileSize/FileHash checks and exact official metadata binding are separate requirements. Nix still validates decompressed signed NarHash/NarSize. This reviewer observed Sig presence, not a completed cryptographic validation.

Nix2.34.8 defaults require-sigs=true, trusted=false for source, and built-in cache.nixos.org-1 public key. Effective local/daemon settings have not been read or confirmed here. Root must establish unchanged required effective signature policy and official public key through narrow safe evidence, without full configuration/auth dumps. Never use no-check-sigs, trusted=true, require-sigs=false, new keys or local signing.

Default nix copy computes entire source closure before destination missing-path filtering. A one-narinfo cache cannot support that traversal even if referenced paths exist in destination; at least source metadata for traversed refs is needed, though already-valid destination refs need not transfer NARs.

--no-recursive is explicitly in installed help and implemented in matching source. It leaves only the target in the item set; topology ignores refs outside that set; destination copies only missing target and registerValidPaths requires every reference valid. Self-reference is normal and is satisfied by registration of target itself. It is not a missing dependency requiring a second copy.

Also supported if every non-self ref is already valid: substitution goals immediately succeed for valid refs before querying source metadata. Missing refs require authentic entries from the only selected cache and otherwise fail. Exact non-.drv target has no derivation to build when substitution is unavailable; no ignore-unknown. A per-command substituters override does not persist config, but introduces a settings distinction avoided by preferred nonrecursive copy. No realise was run.

Preflight exact signed refs against actual destination valid-path registration, not filesystem existence. If any non-self ref is missing, do not start single-object installation. Report exact missing set and prepare authentic official narinfo/complete NARs for necessary missing dependency closure under a new bounded plan, then register dependency-first. Do not synthesize metadata/refs/DB rows, silently fetch another source, remove refs or bypass closure validation.

Parent may choose bounded downloading and hash-validation of public cache regular files while existing setup still runs; this changes no Nix-store registration/settings/flake or existing guard. Use an exclusive directory, partial-file publication discipline, finite deadline, byte/disk bounds and actual receipt/custody. No Nix store-opening/copy/realise/verify should occur until old setup actually terminates/joined and no related competing process remains. Concurrent public downloading can compete for network/disk; its success or speed does not diagnose original setup or extend its guard.

After actual successful native copy/realise and source hash/custody checks, run content+trust verification with no no-contents/no-trust. LLVM narinfo has no CA field, so explicit sigs-needed1 requires a trusted signature rather than ultimate-local-trust shortcut; verify contents reserializes NAR and checks signed NarHash. Preserve actual exit/status and target registration. Verify does not repair missing paths and does not itself prove shell readiness or protocol acceptance.
